subject: Energy
title: What Is Nuclear Energy?
description: A fast breakdown of What Is Nuclear Energy? for builders.

hook.text: Nuclear energy comes from the nucleus of atoms—the tiny core that holds 99.9% of an atom's mass.

buildup.text: The strong nuclear force binds protons and neutrons together—overcoming their electrical repulsion.

discovery.text: When heavy nuclei split (fission) or light nuclei merge (fusion), a fraction of mass converts to enormous energy.

twist.text: Nuclear reactions release millions of times more energy per atom than chemical reactions like burning.

climax.text: One uranium fuel pellet the size of a fingertip holds as much energy as a ton of coal.

punchline.text: Tiny atoms, enormous energy—millions of times more than fire.

quiz.question: Where does nuclear energy come from?
